request_body.raw_goal: Land a job in tech or product management as fast as possible.
request_body.user_context: Just finished NYSC, actively job-hunting. No income yet, living with parents. High urgency — peers are already employed. Has lots of free time to dedicate.

objectives: Develop a specialized technical or product management resume that passes ATS filters and highlights relevant transferable skills from academic or internship experience.
Master the core competencies required for entry-level roles, specifically software development fundamentals or product lifecycle management (SDLC).
Build a targeted portfolio or case study repository demonstrating practical application of product management frameworks or technical capability.
Execute a high-volume, quality-controlled application strategy while optimizing for networking and referral pathways.
Refine interview performance for behavioral, technical, and product sense questions through iterative feedback loops.

proposed_milestones.description: Profile audit and narrative transformation to align past academic and internship experience with entry-level tech or product management benchmarks.
objectives: Reframe NYSC or previous work history into accomplishment-based bullet points using the STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) method.
Create two versions of a resume: one focused on technical engineering skills and one focused on PM requirements (PRDs, user research, feature roadmapping).
Establish an active LinkedIn presence with optimized headline, 'About' section, and project highlights.

proposed_milestones.description: Creation of a demonstration project or case study that serves as proof of work for recruiters.
objectives: For Product Management: Conduct a 'Product Critique' or design a feature proposal for an existing app, documenting user pain points and proposed solutions.
For Tech: Complete a focused coding project using a relevant stack (e.g., React, Python/Django) with a live GitHub repository.
Draft documentation (README files or slide decks) that articulates the 'why' behind design decisions and technical trade-offs.

proposed_milestones.description: Systematic interview preparation focusing on industry-standard case frameworks and behavioral patterns.
objectives: Study the 'Decode and Conquer' or 'Cracking the PM Interview' frameworks for product sense, estimation, and strategy questions.
Practice 'mock' interview questions using the STAR method for behavioral inquiries.
Set up a peer-review system or use platforms like Pramp to conduct timed mock interviews.

proposed_milestones.description: Execution of an outbound sourcing strategy and funnel management.
objectives: Build a tracker for all job applications, tracking response rates, stages, and points of contact.
Implement a cold outreach strategy to recruiters and peers on LinkedIn using tailored networking templates.
Daily ritual of filtering and applying to high-match roles via job boards like Wellfound, LinkedIn, and Y Combinator's Work at a Startup.

success_metrics: Successfully converted at least 15% of job applications into initial recruiter screening calls.
Completed a minimum of 3 full-cycle technical or product management mock interviews with objective performance feedback.
Secured at least one verifiable referral or internal introduction for a target company.
Maintained a consistent application volume of at least 10 high-quality, tailored applications per week.

request_body.raw_goal: Learn SQL and data analytics properly — I keep seeing it in job listings.
request_body.user_context: Wants to add this skill to strengthen job applications. Frames it as urgent. Already submitted a job-search goal this same session.

objectives: Master the retrieval and manipulation of relational data using standard SQL syntax.
Develop proficiency in aggregating and cleaning datasets for analytical purposes.
Learn to apply common analytical frameworks to extract actionable insights from structured data.
Build a portfolio of SQL-based data analysis projects to demonstrate competence to potential employers.

proposed_milestones.description: Establish core SQL querying capability focusing on DQL (Data Query Language) foundations.
objectives: Master SELECT, FROM, WHERE, and logical operators for basic record retrieval.
Implement JOIN operations (INNER, LEFT, FULL) to combine data from multiple normalized tables.
Practice schema navigation to understand relational table structures.

proposed_milestones.description: Implement data aggregation and transformation techniques for meaningful metric extraction.
objectives: Master aggregate functions like COUNT, SUM, AVG, and use GROUP BY/HAVING clauses.
Execute CASE statements and subqueries for conditional data logic and derived columns.
Practice data cleaning by handling null values and casting data types.

proposed_milestones.description: Construct end-to-end data analysis workflows using a local database environment.
objectives: Import raw datasets (CSV/JSON) into a relational database management system like SQLite or PostgreSQL.
Develop a series of analytical queries to answer specific business-oriented questions.
Document query logic and findings to create a project repository suitable for a portfolio.

success_metrics: Completion of a series of SQL coding assessments scoring 80% or higher.
Development of a GitHub repository containing at least three SQL-based analytical projects with documented schema and methodology.
Ability to write complex queries involving multiple joins and window functions without referencing syntax documentation.
Successful execution of a query to extract, transform, and load (ETL) insights from a provided raw dataset.

request_body.raw_goal: Build a portfolio project — a data dashboard or product case study — that I can show in interviews.
request_body.user_context: Wants this done ASAP to support job applications. Already submitted job-search and SQL learning goals today.

objectives: Identify a high-impact dataset or business problem that demonstrates analytical proficiency.
Perform end-to-end data processing, including cleaning, exploration, and feature engineering.
Design a compelling narrative structure to explain the 'why' behind the project findings.
Implement an interactive visualization dashboard or a clean, professional-grade documentation repository.
Optimize project visibility for recruiters and hiring managers in technical interviews.

proposed_milestones.description: Scoping the problem domain and sourcing a high-quality dataset.
objectives: Select a dataset from a credible source like Kaggle, Google Dataset Search, or a public API.
Define 3-5 clear business questions or analytical hypotheses the project will address.
Perform initial exploratory data analysis to verify data integrity and feasibility.

proposed_milestones.description: Executing data cleaning, transformation, and statistical analysis pipelines.
objectives: Normalize and clean data using SQL or Python (Pandas/NumPy) to address missing values and outliers.
Perform feature engineering to create meaningful metrics relevant to the business goal.
Summarize key findings through descriptive statistics and trend analysis.

proposed_milestones.description: Developing the visualization dashboard or technical case study narrative.
objectives: Build an interactive dashboard using tools like Tableau, Power BI, or Streamlit.
Structure the narrative as a 'Situation-Action-Result' case study to highlight technical decision-making.
Design visual elements that effectively communicate complex insights to non-technical stakeholders.

proposed_milestones.description: Packaging the project for public repository and interview readiness.
objectives: Create a README.md file featuring the project context, technical stack, and a summary of key insights.
Push the finalized code or documentation to GitHub/Portfolio site.
Prepare a 2-minute 'elevator pitch' summary of the project's technical challenges and solutions.

success_metrics: The project is hosted and accessible via a live URL or public repository.
The case study includes at least three distinct visualizations that directly support the project's core hypothesis.
All code is documented with comments and follows standard industry formatting (e.g., PEP 8 for Python).
Successfully explain the project methodology and technical trade-offs in a mock interview setting.
